subject: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What I heard from the call:
- Primary concern: intermittent latency spikes that look like "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared endpoints. These are visible mostly during peak windows (you mentioned weekday mornings).
- Traffic profile: approx 50 req/s baseline with bursts to ~200 req/s for short periods; average response ~150 tokens.
- SLO ask: want guidance/guarantee around p99 latency and an approach to minimize tail spikes.
- Security/regulatory: currently cloud-deployed; may evaluate VPC/private deployment later for PHI considerations.

How Redwood can help (short):
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to onboard, strong autoscaling, prefix/KV caching to reduce cost. However, shared pools can experience tail latency under multi-tenant bursty workloads unless routed / configured for isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools you own — predictable throughput, isolation from noisy neighbors, SLA-backed latency targets. Recommended when you need consistent p99 and reserved throughput.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control and network isolation; best for regulated workloads and scenarios that require private control plane or on-prem hardware.

Immediate proposal / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the target p99 SLO you care about (e.g., < 500ms, < 1s)? Also whether short bursts to 200 req/s are expected to persist.
2) I'd like to set up a technical session with Rishi (SE) to map request characteristics exactly (payload sizes, concurrency, KV usage) so we can size a Dedicated pool or provide a config for Hosted with routing and stronger isolation. Suggested times: Tue/Wed next week.
3) I've attached a short one-pager that compares shared vs dedicated for predictable latency (shared-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf).

If the goal is to avoid tail spikes and have predictable p99, Dedicated is usually the simplest direct path. We can also propose an interim short-term mitigation on Hosted (request routing to smaller model variants, autoscale tuning, and prefix caching) while you evaluate Dedicated pricing.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to prioritize.

Best,
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the recap and the one-pager. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The latency spikes are real and reproducible during our morning windows (08:00–10:30 PT). They manifest as p95 jumps to ~800ms and occasional p99s near ~1.6s. The average request is ~150 tokens out, but some of our longer responses reach 400–500 tokens.
- Traffic profile: baseline steady at ~50 req/s; peaks are brief (1–3 minutes) but frequent multiple times per day. We also run a few large batch inference jobs overnight.
- Cost: Dedicated sounds promising but we need to understand unit economics — if Dedicated is sized to handle peaks it may be expensive unless you can recommend autoscaling/burst patterns.

I attached a screenshot of our internal latency dashboard showing the spikes (latency-screenshot.png).

Next: a technical session with your SE (Rishi) would be ideal. We are available Tue 09:00–12:00 PT or Wed 13:00–16:00 PT. Goal of session: get a sizing recommendation (Dedicated reservation vs tuning on Hosted) and a ballpark cost estimate.

Alex Rivera

Subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — shared vs dedicated follow-up

Alex — thanks for the details and the dashboard screenshot, super helpful. Covering your asks below and proposing concrete next steps: 

1) SLOs & isolation:
- From your numbers, Dedicated capacity is the clearest path to guarantee p99 under bursty traffic. A properly sized reserved pool avoids cross-tenant interference and gives predictable tail latency.
- On Hosted, we can improve isolation via routing policies (route critical traffic to less-loaded regions/variants), KV/prefix caching, and more aggressive autoscale thresholds — these help but don't fully eliminate noisy neighbor risk at p99.

2) Autoscale/burst economics:
- We recommend mixing a modest Dedicated baseline (to cover steady-state + small bursts) with short-term burst capacity for large spikes. Redwood Dedicated supports burst policies and configurable autoscale cooldowns to limit cost while improving p99.
- Rishi will bring a sizing worksheet to the call that maps your request profile to GPU vCPU / token throughput and shows cost tradeoffs for baseline vs full-peak reservation.

3) Proposed next steps:
- Tech session w/ Rishi (SE) to run through request logs, sample payloads, and sizing worksheet. Suggested time: Tue 08 Jun 2026 — 09:30 PT. Please confirm.
- I'll prepare a short MAP (mutual action plan) with milestones: PO, POC window on Dedicated, SLA targets, and pricing. Marissa will draft the pricing/contract details post-call.

4) Pre-call ask:
- If you can share a 24–72h request/response log (anonymized) or a short sample of typical requests (payload sizes + concurrency), Rishi can provide a more precise sizing estimate in the session.

I'll hold 09:30 PT on Tue the 8th tentatively — let me know if that works.

Best,
Priyom
